newsitem.title: ITALY: GOLF-LANGER SHADES OLAZABAL TO WIN ITALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LANGER SHADES OLAZABAL TO WIN ITALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Bernhard Langer shot a course record 64 to edge past Jose Maria Olazabal and win the Italian Open on Sunday for his first European Tour title for nearly two years.

The German began the final round three strokes behind Olazabal but his four birdies in the last five holes while the Spaniard collected only pars down the closing stretch earned Langer the title by one stroke.
Langer's eight-under-par final round gave him a 15-under 273 aggregate. Olazabal carded a 68 while Northern Ireland's Darren Clarke took third place on 11-under after a closing 67.

A first prize of 77,897 pounds ($126,000) hauled Langer up to sixth in the Ryder Cup table while Olazabal's second prize of 51,924 pounds ($84,200) took him 10th, sufficient to earn him an automatic place on the Ryder Cup team.

It also put Olazabal in second place in this year's European Tour money list and continued an amazing return since he resumed two months ago after an 18-month layoff with foot problems which had threatened to end his career.

Thirty-nine-year-old Langer's irresistible finish, which brought his 35th European Tour victory, included single putts on each of the last five greens, his final 15ft putt on the 18th from the fringe winning him the title.
"I played with Jose Maria on Monday and Tuesday and I knew he was the man to beat this week because he was putting magnificently," said Langer.
"At the start of the day I thought a 65 or a 66 might have to be my target because of Jose Maria's form, so it's fantastic to shoot the course record when I needed to.
"I switched back to my wooden driver from metal for the last two rounds and it did the trick. It's great to win after nearly two years without a victory on the European Tour."

Olazabal looked to have the tournament sewn up early on, consistently finding birdies every time Langer caught him. But he had to work hard to save pars towards the finish as the German drew level on the 16th and then clinched the tournament on the final hole.
The Spaniard nearly holed out with a chip from a bunker on the last but the ball screwed away from the cup for him to miss the birdie which would have earned the playoff.
"I'm not disappointed because I did not give the tournament away. Bernhard's was an unbelievable round. I felt a 68 would be enough but not with Bernhard in that kind of form," Olazabal said.
